title: 17 משחקים וספרים שיעזרו להם להכיר אותיות ומספרים

stage.need: Letters, rhymes and numbers in the year before first grade. CDC lists 'Counts to 10', 'Names some numbers between 1 and 5 when you point to them' and 'Uses or recognizes simple rhymes' among the 5 year milestones; KidsHealth suggests alphabet books, poetry and pointing out letters; Ramani and Siegler (2008) found number board games raised preschoolers' counting and numeral identification. Games give the counting a reason, books give the words and rhymes.
stage.age_caveat: Ages are approximate: CDC milestones are what most children (75% or more) do by an age, not a deadline. Some 5 year olds count well past 10 and some need more time; the frame says בסביבות and the caption says יש ילדים ש.... Test fixture: assembled from the 13 and 14 Oct 2026 drafts (their products, evidence and slides), so the theme is wider than one real night would choose.

dev_sources.title: Milestones by 5 Years
dev_sources.publisher: CDC, Learn the Signs. Act Early.
dev_sources.quote: Counts to 10 / Names some numbers between 1 and 5 when you point to them / Teach your child to follow rules in games. For example, play simple board games, card games, or Simon Says.
dev_sources.supports: 5 year cognitive milestones (counts to 10; names some numbers between 1 and 5) and the tip to play simple board games and card games. Read today through a page fetch (the CDC site blocks plain curl); the three sentences are quoted as returned, joined with ' / '. The page has no tip about counting games, so the link between games and counting rests on the second source.

dev_sources.title: Promoting broad and stable improvements in low-income children's numerical knowledge through playing number board games
dev_sources.publisher: Ramani & Siegler, Child Development 2008;79(2):375-94, doi:10.1111/j.1467-8624.2007.01131.x (PubMed, NIH)
dev_sources.quote: playing such a game for roughly 1 hr increased low-income preschoolers' (mean age = 5.4 years) proficiency on 4 diverse numerical tasks: numerical magnitude comparison, number line estimation, counting, and numeral identification. / Classmates who played an identical game, except for the squares varying in color rather than number, did not improve on any measure.
dev_sources.supports: Peer reviewed, preschoolers with a mean age of 5.4: about an hour on a linear number board game raised counting, numeral identification and magnitude comparison, and a colour version of the same game did not. Limits: low-income preschoolers, a 1 to 10 linear board, and only the abstract was read (PubMed's own page returned a cookie notice, so the abstract text came from NCBI's abstract service for PMID 18366429). It supports 'number board games give counting practice', not a result from any product here; the slides say practise or help, never a promised outcome.

dev_sources.title: Milestones by 4 Years
dev_sources.publisher: CDC, Learn the Signs. Act Early.
dev_sources.quote: Says sentences with four or more words / Answers simple questions like "What is a coat for?" or "What is a crayon for?" / Play simple games, such as Tic-Tac-Toe or matching games.
dev_sources.supports: 4 year language milestones (sentences of four or more words; answers simple questions about what things are for) plus the tip to play simple games and matching games. Read today in the in-app browser (plain curl gets 403); sentences joined with ' / ' in page order (milestone list, then the tips list). The page does not say board games build vocabulary; it lists games only as a general tip. Milestones are what 75 percent or more of children do by an age.

dev_sources.title: Language Development in Your 4- to 5-Year-Old
dev_sources.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (medically reviewed by Mary L. Gavin, MD, May 2022)
dev_sources.quote: Reading books, singing, playing word games, asking questions, and talking to your kids will help increase vocabulary and improve their listening skills.
dev_sources.supports: Names 'playing word games' and 'asking questions' among everyday ways to support vocabulary at 4 to 5. A general parent explainer, not research on board games; its own wording is 'will help', so our copy must soften it to 'a chance to practise' (no claim that a game causes vocabulary growth).

dev_sources.title: Story Time for Preschoolers
dev_sources.quote: preschoolers still love rhymes. / Alphabet books, counting books, or books with lots of new words are all good choices. / Ask your child to point out letters or words he or she might know. / Encourage your child to "read" to you and praise the attempts.
dev_sources.supports: Supports using rhymes and poems, alphabet books, pointing out letters or words, and letting the child retell the story as playful reading practice at preschool age. It is general parent guidance, not a test of any specific book.

dev_sources.title: Is Your Child Ready to Read?
dev_sources.quote: Don't drill them on letters, numbers, colors, shapes or words. / Let your child set their own pace and enjoy the journey.
dev_sources.supports: Supports a relaxed, child-led tone: interest in letters and listening at story time are signs of readiness, and drilling is discouraged. Used for the caveat that children differ in pace, not for any claim about a book. The quotes are from the fetch tool's extraction of the page.

dev_sources.title: Nursery Rhyme Knowledge and Phonological Awareness in Preschool Children
dev_sources.publisher: Journal of Language and Literacy Education, v7 n1 (via ERIC, Institute of Education Sciences), L. J. Harper, 2011
dev_sources.quote: Phonological awareness is an important precursor in learning to read.
dev_sources.supports: A peer-reviewed study of pre-K children and nursery rhyme instruction; the abstract (all I read, not the full paper) calls phonological awareness an important precursor to learning to read. Small study with English nursery rhymes, so it does not show that any Hebrew book causes a skill; use only for 'rhymes and sound play are an opportunity to practise listening to sounds'.

dev_sources.title: Milestones by 3 Years
dev_sources.publisher: CDC, Learn the Signs. Act Early.
dev_sources.quote: Puts on some clothes by himself, like loose pants or a jacket / Calms down within 10 minutes after you leave her, like at a childcare drop off / Developmental milestones are things most children (75% or more) can do by a certain age. / Encourage your child to solve her own problems with your support.
dev_sources.supports: By 3 most children put on some clothes by themselves and calm down soon after a childcare drop off; CDC suggests encouraging them to solve their own problems with support. Read through a fetch tool because the CDC site returns 403 to curl; the quotes are the page's words as the tool returned them.

dev_sources.title: Developmental Milestones: 3- to 4-Year-Olds
dev_sources.quote: No longer a toddler, your 3-year-old can do more things on their own. / Dresses and undresses self (coat, jacket, shirt) / Because each child develops in their own manner, it's impossible to tell exactly when or how they'll perfect a given skill.
dev_sources.supports: AAP: at 3 children can do more things on their own, including dressing and undressing, and each child develops in their own manner. Quotes read straight from the page HTML.

products.popularity_reasoning: Strong signal: selected and distributed by Sifriyat Pijama in 2021-2022, and two independent Israeli retailers carry it. No bestseller rank found. The Steimatzky price of 25 NIS against a catalogue price of 74 may be a promotion; I record it as shown.
products.developmental_relevance: Leo gets a pen from his dad and, with his mother, finds in it lines, drawings and words (Sifriyat Pijama blurb: 'a story that encourages literacy ahead of the move to first grade'). The most direct fit to early literacy in this set: an opportunity to talk about drawing, writing and words.
products.parent_tip_source: Sifriyat Pijama family pages for the book ('Discussion', 'Illustrations tell their own story'); the question is my own wording.

image.rights_note: No press or media licence statement found on the page; publisher artwork. Treat as rights_unverified and ask the publisher before publishing. Steimatzky 1200x1600 canvas with a white band around the cover, so trim_padding is set.

products.limitations: Age is the Sifriyat Pijama group label (4-6). Copy count is programme-wide. Steimatzky's cover is a landscape format inside a 1200x1600 white canvas, so trim_padding is needed and the visible cover is about 1200x940. Hebrew translator not found. The blurb names the author as אלן סרג' ז'וטאפ (Steimatzky: דיזוטם, Booknet: דיזוטפ), spellings differ between pages. I did not read the book.

image.rights_note: LumeBook's own catalogue cover art for book 51 (the 'girl' variant URL, which shows a boy of about 6 to 7 with a blue backpack), AVIF converted to PNG with sips without changes. The 'boy' variant URL was also downloaded and viewed; it shows a much older teenager, so it was not used.
image.depicts: A smiling boy of about 6 to 7 in a grey T-shirt with a navy backpack stands on a lawn path in front of a red-brick school building in warm morning sun: the idea of starting school. The cover does not show the listening superpower, so the line names starting school first and the listening second, as the site's own text does. No lettering on the cover.

lumebook.connection: Second to last of 17 suggestions (8 games, 8 books and the LumeBook book), between the last two books, in Yarin's format: ספר של LumeBook / סיפור מותאם אישית עם תמונה של הילדים שלכם שבו... Book 51 (ages 4 to 7, starting school and the superpower of listening) fits a carousel about letters and numbers before first grade; the line says what the cover and the site show.

claims.wording_he: משחקים וספרים שיעזרו להם להכיר אותיות ומספרים
claims.supports: CDC 5 years: counts to 10, names some numbers between 1 and 5, uses or recognises simple rhymes; Ramani and Siegler 2008: a linear number board game raised preschoolers' counting and numeral identification; KidsHealth: alphabet books and pointing out letters support early reading.

claims.wording_he: בסביבות גיל 5 הרבה ילדים כבר סופרים עד 10 ומזהים חרוזים פשוטים
claims.supports: CDC 5-year milestones: 'Counts to 10' and 'Uses or recognizes simple rhymes'.

claims.wording_he: משחקים עם מספרים וספרים עם מילים מאפשרים להם לתרגל את זה
claims.supports: CDC 5 years suggests rhyming games and counting in daily play; Ramani and Siegler 2008 on number board games; KidsHealth on alphabet books and poetry. 'An opportunity to practise' is our wording, not a promise.

Kodkod's page: money values of 1 to 5 suited to young children; players pay and collect. Counting small amounts is practice of the CDC 5 year counting milestone; our reading, not a tested effect of this game.

The game is built on runs of consecutive number tiles (Center Toys page: runs or groups). Ordering numerals draws on naming numbers (CDC 5 years) and numeral identification (Ramani and Siegler); our reading.

claims.wording_he: מתרגלים לספור צעדים על לוח ממוספר
claims.supports: Kodkod: reach square 100 with an exact number of steps. The closest product tonight to the number board game in Ramani and Siegler 2008 (theirs was linear, 1 to 10).
Fox Mind's page: the game gives practice in telling apart and matching colours and digits. Naming numbers 1 to 5 is a CDC 5 year milestone.

claims.wording_he: מתרגלים שמות אותיות ומילים שמתחילות בכל אות
claims.supports: KidsHealth: alphabet books and asking the child to point out letters or words they know; CDC 5 years: names some letters. The book is Naomi Shemer's alef-bet song as an illustrated book (Steimatzky blurb); the full book was not read.

claims.wording_he: מתרגלים להקשיב לקצב של שירים ולחזור על שורות
claims.supports: KidsHealth: preschoolers still love rhymes and poems; CDC: simple rhymes. The book is a collection of poems about Uncle Simcha (Sifriyat Pijama blurb); which poems rhyme was not checked.

claims.wording_he: מתרגלים להקשיב לצלילים בשמות ולשחק עם מילים
claims.supports: CDC: rhyming games (what rhymes with cat); KidsHealth: books with lots of new words. The book is about Yoyo who forgets his name and meets many names (Sifriyat Pijama blurb); the full text was not read.

claims.wording_he: סיפור מותאם אישית עם תמונה של הילדים שלכם
claims.supports: Live site, 2026-10-13: upload a photo of the child and add the name; the name is in the text and the child stars in every illustration.

claims.wording_he: שבו הם מתחילים בית ספר ומגלים את כוח ההקשבה
claims.supports: Catalogue book 51 (lumebook.com, 2026-10-13): an encouraging story about starting school and discovering the superpower of listening; the cover shows a child at a school entrance.

claims.wording_he: מתרגלים לדבר על ציור כתיבה ומילים
claims.supports: KidsHealth: ask your child to point out letters or words they might know and encourage them to 'read' to you; HealthyChildren: let your child set their own pace. The book is a story about a pen and the lines, drawings and words inside it (Sifriyat Pijama blurb).

notes: Test fixture for the combined games and books carousel (14 Oct 2026): 9 suggestions, 12 slides, 4 games then 4 books (cut down from 17 after Yarin capped it at 7 to 9), the LumeBook book second to last.
